html:
SMTO-FIL-0035 — A copy step reached the wrong side of the copy

GUID: adaa5251-ac96-4349-b153-4067b5f988cf
Slug: file-invalid-transfer-action
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • During a copy between Gateways, a step meant for the sending computer reached the receiving one, or the other way round. The Gateway refused it and the copy stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand the two Gateways used for the copy, and compare their addresses and Node names; they should be different computers. If both entries lead to the same Gateway, the sending and receiving steps get mixed up.
  3. Use Check for updates on both Gateways. Gateways on different versions may not agree on the order of copy steps.
  4. Only if the file is missing or different, ask SMTO to copy it again. A new request starts a clean copy instead of continuing the confused one.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't keep repeating the copy until they have confirmed what happened at the destination.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway transfer provider rejected a source_* action for a destination (staging) session, or a destination_* action for a source session, under the same run/transfer key.

What this means

  • A transfer session receives a source action for a destination session or a destination action for a source session. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A transfer session receives a source action for a destination session or a destination action for a source session.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare session role and requested action while retaining the original session ownership.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the controller and both Gateways run matching versions and that the source and destination Gateway records do not resolve to the same Gateway process or node (which would share one session table). Query destination_status for the transfer_id and abort or reconcile it before starting a new copy; do not resend the rejected action.
  • Use a supported action for the current transfer session phase.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The action matches the owned source/destination session role.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
